1.note: This is an idiom. Alternate translation: [remember]

1.q: before the days of difficulty come
1.note: Future time is spoken of as if the “days are coming” Alternate translation: [before you experience difficult times] or [before bad things happen to you]

1.q: before the years arrive when you say, “I have no pleasure in them,”
1.note: Future time is spoken of as if “years arrive” Alternate translation: [before you become old when you say, ‘I no longer enjoy being alive,’]

2.q: do this before the light of the sun … after the rain
2.note: Growing old and dying is spoken of as if the sun and moon go dark and dark clouds return. Alternate translation: [do this before it seems to you that the light of the sun … after the rain]

3.note:
# General Information:

The writer describes a house in which various activities stop. This appears to be a metaphor for the human body as it becomes old.

3.q: the women who grind cease because they are few
3.note: Alternate translation: [the women who grind grain stop grinding grain because there are few of them]

4.q: the doors are shut in the street
4.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [people shut the doors that lead to the street]

4.q: when men are startled at the voice of a bird
4.note: It is implied that the voice of the birds startle the men awake. If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [when the voice of a bird startles men awake] (See also: [Active or Passive](ta:figs-activepassive))

4.q: the singing of girls’ voices fades away
4.note: Here “girls” may be a metaphor for the birds. Alternate translation: [the songs of the birds fade away]

5.note: The “almond tree” is a tree that blossoms in the winter with white flowers.
A grasshopper is a large, straight-winged insect with long, jointed back legs that give it the ability to jump a long way. Here it can only drag itself because it has gotten old and weak.

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea behind the word **desires**, you can express the same idea with a verbal form. Alternate translation: [when people no longer desire what they once did naturally]

5.q: Then man goes to his eternal home
5.note: This refers to death. Alternate translation: [Then man goes to the place of the dead forever] or [Then a person dies and never returns to life]

5.q: the mourners go down the streets
5.note: This could mean: (1) that mourners go down the streets to attend a funeral, or (2) that mourners go down the streets to the house of the person who is about to die.

6.note: This is an idiom. Alternate translation: [Remember]

6.q: before the silver cord is cut … or the water wheel is broken at the well
6.note: The writer speaks of dying as if it were one of these various broken items. Death will break the body just as suddenly as people accidentally break these items while they are using them.
If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [someone cuts the silver cord]

If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [someone crushes the golden bowl]
If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [someone shatters the pitcher]

If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [someone breaks the water wheel]

7.note: Here the word “dust” refers to the human body that has decomposed.

8.q: A mist of vapor … everything is vanishing vapor
8.note: The Teacher speaks of things as being useless and meaningless as if they were “vapor.” Just as vapor disappears and does not last, the author speaks of things having no lasting value. See how you translated “vapor” in Ecclesiastes 1:14. Alternate translation: [Temporary and useless … everything is temporary and useless] or [Meaningless … everything is meaningless]
See how you translated this in [Ecclesiastes 1:1](ta:01).

9.note: Alternate translation: [thought much about and arranged] or [thought much about and wrote down]

10.note: The Teacher wanted the words to be pleasurable to the listener. They bring pleasure because they are well written, not because they are comforting.

11.q: The words of wise people … taught by one shepherd
11.note: The writer speaks of the teacher who uses his words to instruct people as if the teacher were a shepherd who uses his tools to lead his flock.

11.q: The words of wise people are like goads
11.note: This is a simile. Alternate translation: [Wise people encourage people to act, like a sharp stick encourages an animal to move]

11.q: Like nails driven deeply are the words of the masters in collections of their proverbs
11.note: This is a simile. Alternate translation: [Like you can depend on a nail that a person drives firmly into a piece of wood, so you can depend on the words of the masters in collections of their proverbs]

11.q: the words of the masters in collections of their proverbs
11.note: Alternate translation: [the wise words collected in their proverbs] or [the sayings of the wise]

11.q: which are taught by one shepherd
11.note: If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [which one shepherd teaches]

12.q: the making of many books, which has no end
12.note: The noun phrase “the making” can be stated as a verb. Alternate translation: [people will never stop making many books]
Here “body” represents the whole person. Alternate translation: [makes the person tired]

13.note: Alternate translation: [The final conclusion on the matter]

If your language does not use the passive form in this way, you can state this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [after you have heard everything]

14.note: Things done in secret is spoken of as if they were an object that was hidden. Alternate translation: [along with everything that people do in secret]
